runs.question: What penalty does the NIST AI RMF set for an organization that chooses not to adopt it?

answer.text:
The AI RMF documents I searched do not set any penalty for organizations that choose not to adopt it. The closest statement is that the framework is optional. The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic, providing flexibility to organizations of all sizes and in all sectors and throughout society to implement the approaches in the Framework.

Because it is voluntary, the framework itself imposes no consequence for declining it. A search of the NIST AI 100-1 document for penalties or non-adoption consequences returned no such provision. I did not check other documents in the collection for this, so I can say only that the AI RMF does not state one.

support.reason: The passage states the same wording: voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, use-case agnostic, flexibility for organizations of all sizes and sectors.
